## Problem E4: Bomb Calorimeter — Combustion of Sucrose {.unnumbered}

Sucrose (table sugar, $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$) is the most common dietary sugar. When metabolised by the body it is ultimately oxidised to $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ — a process energetically equivalent to combustion. Food scientists measure the energy content of foods by burning samples in a bomb calorimeter: the food is ignited inside a sealed steel vessel (the "bomb") filled with oxygen, which is itself immersed in a water bath. The entire assembly sits inside a perfectly insulated outer container. After the reaction is complete, the temperature rise of the water bath is used to determine the enthalpy of combustion.

The following data are provided:

| Species | Enthalpy of formation, $\Delta H^\circ_f$ / kJ mol$^{-1}$ | Heat capacity, $C_P$ / J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ | Molecular weight / g mol$^{-1}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$ (s) | −2222 | 425.5 | 342 |
| $\mathrm{O_2}$ (g) | 0 | 29.4 | 32 |
| $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (g) | −393.5 | 37.1 | 44 |
| $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (g) | −241.8 | 33.6 | 18 |
| $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (l) | −285.8 | 75.4 | 18 |

| Component | Mass / kg | Heat capacity ($C_P$) / kJ kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ |
|---|---|---|
| Steel bomb | 0.5 | 0.49 |
| Water bath | 2.0 | 4.18 |

The bomb is charged with 5$\times$ the stoichiometric quantity of oxygen. Mass of sucrose sample: 20 g. The system starts at 298.15 K.

**(a)** Write the balanced combustion reaction for sucrose.

**(b)** Calculate the enthalpy of reaction ($\Delta H^\circ_{rxn}$) at 298.15 K with $\mathrm{H_2O}$(g) as the product.

**(c)** Starting from the general energy balance, write down and simplify the energy balance that describes what happens inside the bomb calorimeter from ignition until the system reaches its final temperature.

**(d)** Calculate the final temperature of the entire system (bomb and water bath).

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions"}

::: {.callout-note icon=false collapse="true" title="Solution"}

**(a) Balanced combustion reaction**

$$\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} + 12\,\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 12\,\text{CO}_2 + 11\,\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**(b) Enthalpy of reaction at 298.15 K, with $\mathrm{H_2O}$(g) as product**

$$\Delta H^\circ_{rxn} = \sum \nu_j\,\Delta H^\circ_{f,j} = 12(-393.5) + 11(-241.8) - (-2222) - 0$$

$$\Delta H^\circ_{rxn} = -4722 - 2659.8 + 2222 = -5159.8\ \text{kJ/mol}$$

$$\Delta H^\circ_{rxn} \approx -5160\ \text{kJ/mol} \quad \text{(strongly exothermic)}$$

Note: This is the value per mole of sucrose reacted.

**(c) Simplified energy balance**

Assumptions and simplifications:

- Perfectly insulated outer container $\Rightarrow \dot{Q} = 0$.
- Sealed vessel, no flow in or out $\Rightarrow$ all $\dot{m}H$ terms are zero.
- No work is done $\Rightarrow \dot{W} = 0$.
- Integrating the balance from ignition to final equilibrium $\Rightarrow \Delta H_{sys} = 0$ over the process.

Starting from the general energy balance:

$$\frac{d(m_{sys}H_{sys})}{dt} =\sum \dot{m}_{in}H_{in} - \sum \dot{m}_{out}H_{out}  + \dot{Q} + \dot{W}$$

with the flow terms and $\dot{Q}$, $\dot{W}$ all zero, so:
$$\frac{d(m_{sys}H_{sys})}{dt}=0$$
$$ d(m_{sys}H_{sys}) = 0\,dt$$
$$ \int^f_i d(m_{sys}H_{sys}) = 0 $$
$$ m_{sys}\int^f_i dH_{sys} = 0 $$
$$ m_{sys}\,\Delta H_{sys} = 0 $$
$$ \Delta H_{sys} = 0 $$

Following a reaction-then-heat path (react at 298.15 K, then bring everything to $T_f$), this becomes:

$$\Delta H_{sys} = n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15} + \sum n_j\,C_{P,j}\,(T_f - T_i) + \sum m_k\,C_{P,k}\,(T_f - T_i) = 0$$

where the first sum runs over the gas-phase species in the bomb (combustion products plus excess $\mathrm{O_2}$), and the second sum runs over the steel bomb and the water bath.

**(d) Final temperature**
To calculate the final temperature, solve:

$$n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15} + \sum n_j\,C_{P,j}\,(T_f - T_i) + \sum m_k\,C_{P,k}\,(T_f - T_i) = 0$$
$$\sum n_j\,C_{P,j}\,(T_f - T_i) + \sum m_k\,C_{P,k}\,(T_f - T_i) = - n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15}$$
$$(T_f - 298.15) (\sum n_j\,C_{P,j} + \sum m_k\,C_{P,k}) = - n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15}$$
$$T_f - T_i = \frac{- n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15}}{\sum n_j\,C_{P,j} + \sum m_k\,C_{P,k}}$$
$$T_f = \frac{- n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15}}{\sum n_j\,C_{P,j} + \sum m_k\,C_{P,k}} + T_i$$


Moles of sucrose:

$$n_{sucrose} = \frac{20}{342} = 0.05848\ \text{mol}$$

Stoichiometric $\mathrm{O_2}$ required: $12 \times 0.05848 = 0.7018$ mol. Total $\mathrm{O_2}$ charged (5$\times$ stoichiometric): $3.509$ mol. Excess $\mathrm{O_2}$: $3.509 - 0.7018 = 2.807$ mol.

Products formed: $\mathrm{CO_2}$ $= 0.7018$ mol; $\mathrm{H_2O}$(g) $= 11 \times 0.05848 = 0.6433$ mol.

"Heat" released by the reaction:

$$n_{sucrose} \times \Delta H^\circ_{rxn} = 0.05848 \times  -5159.8 = - 301.745 \ \text{kJ}$$

{{< pagebreak >}}

Heat capacity contributions of everything that must be warmed from 298.15 K to $T_f$:

| Component | $\mathbf{n}$ or $\mathbf{m}$ | $\mathbf{C_P}$ | $\mathbf{nC_P}$ or $\mathbf{mC_P}$ (kJ/K) |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (g) | 0.7018 mol | 0.0371 kJ mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ | 0.026 |
| $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (g) | 0.6433 mol | 0.0336 kJ mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ | 0.022 |
| Excess $\mathrm{O_2}$ (g) | 2.807 mol | 0.0294 kJ mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ | 0.082 |
| Steel bomb | 0.5 kg | 0.49 kJ kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ | 0.245 |
| Water bath | 2.0 kg | 4.18 kJ kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ | 8.360 |
| **Total** | | | **8.735** |

The gas-phase heat capacity contribution ($0.130$ kJ/K) is only about 1.5% of the total, so it is reasonable to neglect it, simplifying the total to $\sum m_k C_{P,k} = 8.605$ kJ/K (steel bomb + water bath only). Using the full total of 8.735 kJ/K:

$$\Delta T = \frac{- n_{surcose}\,\Delta H_{rxn,298.15}}{\sum(n_jC_{P,j} + m_kC_{P,k})} = \frac{301.745}{8.735} = 34.54\ \text{K}$$

$$T_f = 298.15 + 34.54 = 332.69\ \text{K}$$

$$T_f = 332.69\ \text{K} \ (59.5\ ^\circ\text{C})$$
:::
:::
